title: Redaction-fallback & replay-safe ingest processor for console analytics
creator: Marco Liu
description: We need a robust ingestion-side processor for console telemetry that: (1) applies deterministic PII redaction/tokenization at ingest, (2) gracefully falls back for unparseable or schema-variant events without losing ability to delete/replay, and (3) emits tombstone-aware outputs for downstream consumers. Current pipeline scrubbing happens in multiple downstream jobs and lacks a deterministic mapping between original event and scrubbed artifact, which complicates selective erase requests and replays. This ticket scopes a new stateless+stateful hybrid ingest processor that standardizes redaction rules, records a compact delete-key for each event, and supports replay-safe transformations and backfills. The deliverable includes the service, migration/backfill plan, dashboarding for failure modes, and an ops runbook.
proposed_solution: Build a new ingest microservice (ingest-redact) that sits between the ingestion frontdoor (kafka topic ingress) and the main analytics topic. The service will: 1) run a fast schema detection and apply per-schema redaction rules (field-level allowlists + deterministic tokenization using HMAC with per-tenant salt stored in KMS); 2) emit two downstream variants: (a) scrubbed event for analytics consumers and (b) compact delete-key record (immutable) written to a retention-index topic for deletion coordination; 3) for events that fail parsing or match unknown schema, write a flagged tombstone record with original payload checksum and minimal metadata so replays/backfills can reprocess; 4) expose a small metadata index (compact protobuf messages) with mapping from event-id to tokenized identifiers to enable selective erase without scanning raw payloads. Use Rust-based pipeline for perf. Leverage existing KMS integration for tenant salts and add audit log entries for each redaction decision. Implement feature flags to route a percentage of traffic to the new processor for canary testing.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest-redact service deployed to staging and able to process 10k eps with median <50ms per event transformation
Deterministic tokenization produced identical tokens for same PII and tenant across restarts (HMAC salt rotation handled)
Tombstone records emitted on parse failures containing checksum + schema-hint without exposing PII
Downstream consumers receive scrubbed events and delete-index topic contains compact delete-keys with event-id mapping
Canary routing and rollback via feature flag in console deployed and tested
Operational runbook created with SLOs, alert thresholds, common failure triage steps, and a backfill plan
steps: Design review: finalize schema detection heuristics and redaction rule language (Confluence doc)
Implement prototype Rust transformer + HMAC tokenization using KMS-wrapped salts
Add tombstone/delete-index topic writers and compact protobuf schema
Deploy canary in staging with 1% traffic, validate metrics and audit logs
Run controlled backfill for last 30 days in staging using replay harness
Gradual ramp to 25%/50%/100% across regions, monitor SLOs and consumer compatibility
Post-migration: deprecate legacy downstream scrubs and update consumer contracts
